references.text: Describes the right of the priest's family to eat from the holy offerings in their purity
The immediate context defining who may and may not eat from the holy offerings, including the priest's daughter who is married to a foreigner
Parallel legislation regarding who in the priest's household may eat from the holy offerings
Mentions widows and divorced women in connection with priests' marriages
Ezekiel repeats regulations concerning priests marrying widows, relating to the status of the priest's daughter
Tamar returns to her father's house as a widow, a similar pattern where a daughter returns to her father's home
Ruth is urged to return to her mother's house as a widow, a parallel situation to that of the priest's daughter
